Technical Manual
:::

## Definitive small-number rule

BNR suppresses a count when **n < 6**. The directly identifying frequencies are
therefore 1â€“5. Zero is not a small positive count, but it must still be reviewed
in context.

Suppression is a release-level control, not only a cell-formatting rule. Review
the complete set of related public datasets, tables, charts, narrative and
downloads.

## Required review

1. Confirm that every count from 1 to 5 is suppressed in the proposed public output.
2. Check whether totals, subtotals, percentages, rates, complements or repeated
   views allow a suppressed count to be derived.
3. Apply complementary suppression or remove a related calculated value where
   needed to prevent deduction.
4. Check chart labels, tooltips, annotations, downloadable data and narrative.
5. Record the human disclosure decision against the exact candidate.
6. Rebuild through code if the candidate is unsafe; do not edit the generated file.

## Workflow boundary

The event and mortality workflows implement product-specific deterministic
suppression and create private review material. Annual and one-off reports
require review of their complete PDF and landing-page candidate. The rolling
update may display only the protected values supplied by approved public metric
releases and the transformations authorised by its controlled template.

Quarto must not reverse suppression, infer protected components or substitute a
new disclosure-control rule. Public CVD tables reuse the disclosure-controlled
approved metric releases.

## Stop conditions

Do not approve or publish when a value from 1 to 5 is visible, a protected value
can be derived, an unavailable component has been inferred, or the disclosure
review is incomplete.
